question.text: A moving coil galvanometer has 50 turns and each turn has an area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> . The magnetic field produced by the magnet inside the galvanometer is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0.02</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> . The torsional constant of the suspension wire is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mi>rad</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> . When a current flows through the galvanometer, a full scale deflection occurs if the coil rotates by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0.2</mn><mi> </mi><mi>rad</mi></math> . The resistance of the coil of the galvanometer is <math><mn>50</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> . This galvanometer is to be converted into an ammeter capable of measuring current in the range <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>1.0</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> . For this purpose, a shunt resistance is to be added in parallel to the galvanometer. The value of this shunt resistance, in ohms, is __________.
